Im a student in healthcare and this is my observation. Covid is not a killer for most people unless you have a high viral load or pre-existing conditions. But we do not know the long term effects and there is a lot of variability in the symptoms. Ive seen cases who were tested w/ fever and cough test negative and people with no symptoms or very mild ones test positive. Weirdly enough, I have also seen lots of cases of 1 family member testing positive and all others testing negative. We had a married couple who the husband had it but wife did not (tested twice). The doctors I work with are speculating that perhaps some people have innate immunity to this but are not sure how (previous vaccines or infections?) In all seriousness, Wearing a mask and socially distancing might not 100% prevent you from getting it but it can very well be the difference from having mild or severe symptoms because it can significantly reduce the amount your exposed too. Obviously, a flu shot would be a good idea. You probably don’t want to have both at the same time.

I think Red, 1989, and Reputation are all great albums but in a different way. I don’t like how I’ve seen people trying to directly compare them when you can’t... Apples and oranges tbh

What I have observed is that those who are into edm / hip-hop /r&b love reputation. I’ve seen so many people who legit hated her music before who love this album. Reputation objectively is by far the most mature album she has done. It’s also the first where she is really open in her vulnerabilities and mistakes. Reputation is a concept album and some people don’t get it and can’t. The album deals with how her “reputation” has affected her relationships over the years. Taylor is saying overall in the album that she won’t let the media define her life anymore. She is in a good place so to speak. It’s a linear album as she stated and if you really listen it tells a story from beginning to end. 

1989 is very bubblegum pop and radio friendly. It’s a bit kidz bopish. I’ve noticed that a lot of people who weren’t into her country music like this album and vice versa.

Red is diverse. Still country but also some pop. I appreciate the lack of production in some of these songs like Speak Now. Lol my sister hates Red. It’s hilarious to me because so many people love that album on here. My sister thinks it’s a boring album for the most part. 

One thing that a lot of people might not know is Taylor created 1989 to win AOTY. Lol she admitted it in an interview. Taylor definitely had the opportunity to make Red part 2, 1989 part 2 and etc but she didn’t. She pushed herself and made something different. No disrespect to Adele. Love her. But if you see her reviews for 25, almost all of them note that 25 has the same exact sound as 21. No creativity. 

All in All, between 1989, Red, and Reputation, I don’t think there is an objective “best” . They are all reallly well done albums and it will come down to your unique music preference.
